title: Bhakti yoga: the nine forms of devotion; the Alvars and Nayanars; Mirabai, Tulsidas, Surdas; kirtan as method (1 of 7)
hook: a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water: the road that runs on love
tomorrow: Bhakti yoga: the nine forms of devotion; the Alvars and Nayanars; Mirabai, Tulsidas, Surdas; kirtan as method (2 of 7)

segments.voice: Last week: karma yoga, and one line to carry it, offer the work. The birds, the butcher, the curly tail, the half-golden mongoose. Did a small gift go unmentioned? Today, the second of the three paths. Day two hundred sixty-seven.

Think about the last time you did something ridiculous for someone you love. Drove two hours for a birthday. Learned a song on the guitar, badly, for a wedding. Kept a voicemail for years because of the voice on it. Nobody asked you to. It didn't make sense on paper. It was love, and love has its own logic. Most of the world's Hindus, if you asked them what their religion feels like from the inside, wouldn't start with philosophy or with duty. They'd start here. With love, aimed at God. Today: bhakti.
screen: `SOMETHING RIDICULOUS FOR LOVE.` → `IT DIDN'T MAKE SENSE ON PAPER.` → `LOVE, AIMED AT GOD.`

segments.voice: Bhakti comes from the Sanskrit root bhaj: to share, to take part in, to belong to, and so to love and worship. Bhakti is a sharing. You belong to God, and God, in the bhakti picture, lets you in. The Narada Bhakti Sutra, a short classic of the devotional path, begins by defining it simply: bhakti is supreme love for God. Not an idea about God. Love. And in the Gita, Krishna says what that love can look like. Paraphrased: whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water, that offering of love I accept. A leaf. The cheapest thing in the world. That verse is why a single marigold at a roadside shrine counts. The karma path asked: what do you do? The bhakti path asks: who do you love, and how? Then the Puranas tell a story about a boy who knew the answer. Prahlada was the son of a demon king, Hiranyakashipu, who hated Vishnu and wanted his son raised to hate him too. One day the king sat the boy on his lap and asked: tell me the best thing your teachers taught you. And the little boy, in his father's lap, gave the wrong answer on purpose. He listed nine ways of loving Vishnu. Hearing about him. Singing about him. Remembering him. And six more, which we'll open tomorrow. The king was furious. Prahlada didn't budge. Love as the road, even when the road runs through your own father's house.
screen: `BHAJ — TO SHARE, TO BELONG.` · `SUPREME LOVE FOR GOD.` · `A LEAF, A FLOWER, A FRUIT, WATER.` · `PRAHLADA'S WRONG ANSWER.` · then, large: `LOVE AS THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: Sit, and bring to mind someone or something you love without needing a reason. A person, a place, a child's laugh, a piece of music. Feel it in the chest, not the head. Breathe in, and let that warmth grow a little. Breathe out, and notice it wants to go somewhere, to give. If you pray, you can let it turn toward God as you know God, like a leaf set down at a shrine. If you don't, just let the love be there, simple and whole. The bell holds the time.
Bhakti yoga. Devotion as a path: from bhaj, to share and belong. Love for God, offered as simply as a leaf, a flower, a fruit, a little water.
Your line: love as the road. Today, do one small thing for someone purely out of love, the leaf-and-flower kind, cheap and wholehearted. Day two hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: For many Hindus, bhakti is the heart of daily religious life: offering flowers, water, food or a lamp to a chosen form of God at home or in the temple, singing devotional songs, and repeating a divine name.

fork.setup: you're Prahlada, a little boy in the lap of your father, a king who hates Vishnu. he asks: what's the best thing your teachers taught you? what do you say?
fork.reveal: he lists nine ways of loving Vishnu, hearing, singing, remembering and six more, knowing his father will be furious.

original.note: Sanskrit: bhakti, devotion; from the root bhaj, to share, partake, belong to, worship.

trapdoor: what you thought: bhakti is just emotional religion.
what it means: a full path to God through love, as serious as the paths of action and knowledge.

what a scholar hears: the root bhaj means to share or partake; the Gita (esp. ch. 9 and 12) and later the Bhagavata Purana and Narada Bhakti Sutra made devotion a complete path, and bhakti movements reshaped Hindu life across India from the Tamil saints onward.
